column2: The top bead is worth 5. Each bottom bead is worth 1. A bead counts when it touches the bar.
When there are enough beads, just push them to the bar. No tricks yet.
If the beads are already at the bar, just push them away.
Not enough 1-beads? Use the 5-bead and take away its small friend. 1↔4 and 2↔3 are small friends: they make 5.
Need to take away but the 1-beads are not there? Take away the 5-bead and add back its small friend.
Not enough room on the rod? Add 10 on the next rod and take away the big friend. 1↔9, 2↔8, 3↔7, 4↔6, 5↔5 make 10.
Same trick with smaller numbers: add 10, take away the big friend.
Not enough beads to take away? Take 10 from the next rod and add back the big friend.
Same trick with smaller numbers: take 10, add back the big friend.
Adding 6, 7, 8 or 9 and the big friend will not come off? Use the small friend inside the big-friend move. Taking away works the same way. Two tricks, one move.
Work left to right: tens rod first, then units. Every rod uses the same friends.
Picture the beads in your head. Numbers flash by; move the beads in your mind; say the answer.
Long rows use every friend you know. Keep going number after number, keep your finger on your place, and let the beads do the thinking.
Five two-digit numbers in a row. Tens rod first, then units. When the tens rod is full, a big friend carries onto the hundreds rod.
Same mental beads, more numbers. Picture the abacus, add each number as it flashes, and keep the picture still between numbers.
Now three rods for each number: hundreds, tens, units. Always start on the left. Each rod is just a one-digit sum you already know.
3 × 4 means three 4s: 4, 8, 12. Count up on the abacus to see it, then learn the answer by heart. Fast facts make abacus multiplying easy.
The bigger tables. 3 × 7 is three 7s: 7, 14, 21. Count up a few times, then say the fact without counting.
Picture two rods now: tens and units. Add the tens first, then the units, just like on the real abacus.
Thousands, hundreds, tens, units: four rods for each number. Left to right, one rod at a time, every friend still works.
Start at 0. Go left to right: times each digit by the small number and add the answer to the abacus. Every times answer takes two rods.
Same method, one more digit: hundreds, then tens, then units. A 0 digit gives 00, so nothing to add: just move one rod right.
First we meet the beads. Sums come soon!
